wu: Tech Charades: Students draw tech words (e.g., 'smartphone', 'social media') from a hat and act them out while others guess. Winner gets a point.
wuAlt: Tech Pictionary: Students sketch tech devices and classmates name them.
Tech Word Association: Teacher says 'phone', students shout related words like 'call', 'app', 'screen'.
pres: Show flashcards of teens using tech (e.g., 'studying with a laptop', 'scrolling on TikTok'). Model sentences: 'I like studying with my laptop', 'She hates scrolling on TikTok'. Check understanding with thumbs up/down for 'Do you like using your phone?'
presAlt: Realia Tech Talk: Bring in old phones/keyboards. Students describe their habits using 'I love/hate + -ing'.
Tech Survey: Students ask 3 classmates 'Do you like/hate using ___?' and report back.
prac: Verb Pattern Match: Students match 'like/love/hate' cards to '-ing' verb cards (e.g., 'like' → 'playing games'). Play in pairs, then swap cards for a new round.
pracAlt: Tech Habit Survey: Students walk around asking 'Do you like/hate + -ing?' and tally responses.
Sentence Race: Teams race to write 5 correct sentences using 'like/love/hate + -ing'.
ls: Listen to a 1-minute debate: 'Is social media good for teens?'. Students tick arguments for/against and underline 2 'if-clauses' (e.g., 'If you use it too much, you can lose sleep').
re: Tech Freeze: Teacher shouts tech words (e.g., 'laptop!', 'phone!'). Students freeze and say a full sentence like 'I love using my laptop!' to unfreeze.
prod: Debate Carousel: Teams debate 'Should phones be allowed in school?' using 'I think...', 'If we allow phones,...', 'I agree because...' with 2-min turns. Rotate opponents.
rw: Read a short debate text about 'Are robots helpful?'. Circle all 'if-clauses' and write 2 sentences: 'If robots do our jobs, humans might be lazy' and 'If we use robots, we can save time'.
st: Watch a 2-minute animated story about a teen balancing screen time and homework. Close with: 'Today we debated tech opinions using like/love/hate + -ing and conditionals. Thanks for your great ideas, class!'
g: Students describe tech words without saying 'phone', 'screen', or 'app'
Start with 'If I use my phone too much...', next student adds 'I might get bad grades'
Bingo cards with tech habits; mark off when someone says 'I love/hate + -ing'
Roll dice to get debate topics (e.g., 'Social media', 'Video games')
diff: Fast finishers: Write a 5-sentence paragraph about their ideal tech device.
Support: Use sentence frames: 'I like/hate + ___. If I ___, I might ___.'
hw: Record a 90-second video saying your opinion: 'Do you like/hate using AI? Why? Use 2 'if-clauses'.
Write 5 sentences about your family's tech habits using like/love/hate + -ing.
Interview 3 people: 'Do you think robots will replace jobs? Why?' and write their answers.
tip: Encourage polite arguing with phrases like 'I understand your point, but...' to mirror real debates. Link to local tech habits (e.g., 'In Morocco, many families use WhatsApp for calls').
